42853323.text: Localized intrahepatic bile duct dilatation (LIBD) is a prevalent radiological finding characterized by a variety of etiologies, including congenital anomalies, inflammatory conditions, hepatolithiasis, and neoplastic lesions. Accurate differential diagnosis of diseases associated with LIBD is crucial for formulating appropriate treatment strategies and improving patient prognosis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the definitions, etiologies, clinical symptoms, and key imaging features of common diseases associated with LIBD. Furthermore, it proposes a structured approach for differential diagnosis. By integrating imaging findings with clinical and laboratory data, this approach aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and assist radiologists in making optimal clinical decisions. KEY POINTS: Question LIBD has diverse etiologies and overlapping imaging patterns, but a practical, standardized radiological framework for differential diagnosis remains lacking. Findings This pictorial review summarizes characteristic CT/MRI findings of common LIBD-associated diseases and establishes a stepwise diagnostic approach integrating obstruction points, morphology, and clinical information. Critical Relevance Statement By combining specific imaging patterns with clinical context, this review provides a practical differential diagnostic framework that may improve diagnostic confidence, guide further evaluation, and facilitate earlier detection of malignant transformation in LIBD.

42912573.text: A 79-year-old man underwent proton beam therapy (PBT) for hepatocellular carcinoma. During follow-up, MRI demonstrated stable T2-weighted hyperintensity in the irradiated region without interval enlargement or mass formation. Five years after PBT, a new hepatocellular carcinoma developed elsewhere in the liver. 18 F-FDG PET showed no apparent abnormal uptake in the irradiated region, whereas 18 F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-74 PET demonstrated persistent uptake. These findings may reflect chronic radiation-induced fibroinflammatory changes and suggest that fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-PET can visualize such changes even years after PBT.

42950523.label: Purpose
42950523.text: Recently, a single-source photon-counting detector (PCD-CT) system with detector settings comparable to the dual-source system has been introduced. Although applicable to coronary CT angiography (CCTA), its lower temporal resolution may lead to more pronounced motion and misalignment artefacts. Image slab misalignment correction algorithm reduces these artefacts; therefore, we aimed to evaluate its effect on subjective image quality metrics on this PCD-CT system.

42950523.label: Methods
42950523.text: CCTA images were reconstructed with and without using misalignment correction algorithm. Four readers with varying experience evaluated coronary vessels using three image quality metrics: motion, misalignment artefact, and diagnostic confidence. Linear mixed-effect models were used to assess the effects of reconstruction type, image quality metrics, vessels, and readers. To assess reader agreement, intraclass correlation and multiple agreement metrics were used.

42950523.label: Results
42950523.text: 102 patients (53.9% female) were included in the final analysis. The type of reconstruction significantly affected image quality metric scores (p = 0.031). Post-hoc analysis showed that misalignment corrected reconstruction significantly improved misalignment artefacts (Δ = 0.94, 95% CI, 0.88-0.99, p < 0.01) and diagnostic confidence (Δ = 0.296, 95% CI, 0.24-0.36, p < 0.01). Misalignment correction showed a more modest effect on motion artefacts (Δ = 0.065, 95% CI, 0.008-0.122, p = 0.026). Inter-rater reliability was good for both reconstruction types (ICC = 0.713 and ICC = 0.657 for original dataset and corrected dataset). Agreement with the most experienced reader improved using misalignment correction (Exact agreement with the least experienced reader: 43.3% and 54.1%).

42950523.label: Conclusion
42950523.text: The correction algorithm reduced misalignment artefacts and enhanced subjective diagnostic confidence on single-source PCD-CT, with benefits observed across readers of varying experience.

42957873.label: Background
42957873.text: 18F-SynVesT-1 is a PET tracer targeting synaptic vesicle protein 2A, a surrogate marker of synaptic density. Simplified quantification using pseudo-reference regions such as the centrum semiovale (CSO) or whole cerebellum (CER) has previously been validated in healthy volunteers and Alzheimer's disease. This study assessed how motion correction and white-matter hyperintensities (WMH) affect 18F-SynVesT-1 quantification. We reconstructed 18F-SynVesT-1 images for 40 healthy volunteers and 31 patients with Alzheimer's disease 60-90 minutes post-injection with 3 motion handling methods: no motion correction; 5 minute frame-based post-reconstruction coregistration and averaging, and a high-temporal-resolution data-driven motion correction applied during reconstruction. WMH were segmented from T2-FLAIR images and excluded from the CSO to generate lesion-corrected CSO regions. A region-based voxelwise partial volume correction was applied. SUV and SUVRCSO/CER were compared across motion- and lesion-handling methods and the effects on group differentiation were explored.

42957873.label: Results
42957873.text: Data-driven motion correction during reconstruction improved visual image sharpness and increased SUV in high-binding cortical regions (median +0.3-1.0%, p≤0.001) while reducing SUV in the low-binding CSO (median -0.5%, p=0.001). Coregistering and averaging of frames only increased contrast when there was severe motion. The cerebellum was one of the least affected regions by motion correction (median SUV +0.4% with PETDDLM, p<0.001). WMH affected CSO SUV only when ≥25% of the region contained lesions and never affected the cerebellar SUV. SUVRCSO yielded better group differentiation than SUVRCER after accounting for motion and WMH. Individual patients' z-scores differed significantly in both directions depending on the use of SUVRCSO or SUVRCER (e.g. mean absolute difference of 1.00± 0.82 in the precuneus).

42957873.label: Conclusion
42957873.text: Data-driven motion correction during reconstruction reduced the impact of head movements and attenuation mismatches, improving image contrast and quantitative accuracy. SUVRCER was less sensitive to motion and WMH than SUVRCSO, indicating greater robustness. When motion and WMH effects were controlled, SUVRCSO provided slightly better group differentiation than SUVRCER. These findings suggest that CSO may be preferred for group comparisons in well-controlled datasets, while the cerebellum represents a more robust reference region in the presence of motion or substantial WMH burden. The study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05384353), first posted on 20 May 2022.

43003323.label: Purpose
43003323.text: Health-related social needs (HRSNs), such as food insecurity or transportation difficulties, may affect breast cancer screening and follow-up. We assessed the use of screening mammography (SM) encounters to identify HRSNs and the association between the presence of any HRSN and adherence to recommended breast imaging.

43003323.label: Methods
43003323.text: Women presenting for SM received an optional questionnaire assessing desire for assistance with 8 HRSNs. Demographic and imaging data were extracted for each respondent. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with adherence.

43003323.label: Results
43003323.text: 86% (1463/1704) of women completed the questionnaire, of whom 244 (17%) reported ≥1 HRSN. HRSNs were more common with younger age (p=0.0009), as well as non-White race, Hispanic/Latino ethnicity, non-English primary language, and Medicaid/MassHealth (all p<0.0001). Among women with BI-RADS 1 or 2 index SMs, subsequent SM adherence was lower with ≥1 HRSN (73% vs 87%; p<0.0001). Among women with BI-RADS 0 index SMs, diagnostic imaging adherence was 76% with ≥1 HRSN compared with 95% without HRSNs (p=0.05). On multivariable analysis, ≥1 HRSN was independently associated with lower odds of breast imaging adherence (aOR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.40-0.83). Among women who completed recommended imaging, median (IQR) time to follow-up did not differ by HRSN status for BI-RADS 1 or 2 (366 [363,370] vs 366 [364,378] days; p=0.16) or BI-RADS 0 (30 [15,37] vs 30 [13,130] days; p=0.61).

43003323.label: Conclusions
43003323.text: SM encounters can be used to identify HRSNs. Women reporting ≥1 HRSN were less likely to adhere to breast imaging recommendations, suggesting that HRSN screening during mammography may identify women at increased risk of non-adherence.

43019223.text: Prostate cancer metastasis to the spermatic cord is exceedingly rare. A 64-year-old man with a history of robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy for high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma (pT3b, Gleason 3+5=9) originating from a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left prostate hemisphere presented with biochemical recurrence (PSA: 3.77 ng/mL) 6 years postoperatively. Whole-body 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT revealed a solitary, hypermetabolic nodular mass in the contralateral (right) spermatic cord (SUVmax: 23.0), without local or distant metastasis. Surgical excision confirmed metastatic prostatic adenocarcinoma. This case highlights the crucial role of 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT in detecting atypical soft tissue oligometastases and underscores a potential contralateral dissemination mechanism via pelvic vascular collaterals.

43019573.label: Purpose
43019573.text: This study aims to evaluate the clinical feasibility of 68Ga-nitroimidazole-FAPI (NI-FAPI), targeting both hypoxia and fibroblast activation protein (FAP), in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT.

43019573.label: Methods
43019573.text: Thirty-two patients with gastrointestinal tumors (21 for initial staging, 11 for restaging) underwent both 68Ga-NI-FAPI and 18F-FDG PET/CT within 1 week. Immunohistochemistry for FAP and hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) was performed. Semiquantitative parameters including SUVmax, TBR, MTV, and total lesion FAP expression/glycolysis (TLF/TLG) were compared. Correlations between SUVmax and primary tumor depth, the short diameter of involved lymph nodes, and liver metastases were analyzed.

43019573.label: Results
43019573.text: Immunohistochemistry confirmed FAP expression on cancer-associated fibroblasts and HIF-1α in tumor cytoplasm. 68Ga-NI-FAPI upgraded initial staging in 2 patients (9.52%). Among recurrent patients, its true positive rate was 100% versus 70% for 18F-FDG. 68Ga-NI-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher SUVmax and TBR in primary tumors (14.06±6.26 vs. 10.04±6.53, P=0.005; 12.30±6.80 vs. 6.52±4.38, P<0.001), particularly in signet-ring cell carcinoma (SRCC). It detected more metastases than 18F-FDG (306 vs. 263, P=0.003), with higher SUVmax and TBR in involved lymph nodes, liver metastases, peritoneal metastases, and other distant metastases (all P<0.05). SUVmax of 68Ga-NI-FAPI positively correlated with primary tumor depth (r=0.528, P=0.003), the short diameter of involved lymph nodes (r=0.304, P=0.032), and liver metastases (r=0.349, P=0.040).

43019573.label: Conclusion
43019573.text: 68Ga-NI-FAPI exhibits superior diagnostic performance in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG, particularly in staging, SRCC evaluation, and metastasis detection. The positive correlation between tumor size and uptake supports its potential for patient selection in ligand-directed radionuclide therapy, establishing it as an effective theranostic agent for gastrointestinal tumors.

43025623.label: Introduction
43025623.text: Although myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is a powerful marker of prognosis in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (PET MPI), MFR cannot distinguish between epicardial and microvascular disease. Integrated MFR (iMFR) has been proposed to better detect epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) by combining MFR with focal perfusion abnormalities.

43025623.label: Methods
43025623.text: We studied 34,761 patients as part of the REFINE PET registry of patients undergoing 82Rb or 13N-ammonia PET MPI. A subset of the above population without prior CAD (N=2,869) had a diagnostic angiogram within 180 days of PET MPI. Regions with an MFR <2 and a regional perfusion defect by total perfusion deficit (TPD) were defined as 'focally impaired' on a pixel by pixel basis. Regions with an MFR <2 without a regional perfusion defect were defined as 'diffusely impaired'. We also evaluated a separate angiographic cohort imaged with a third tracer, 18F-flurpiridaz, in the Flurpiridaz-301 trial (N=231). iMFR metrics were evaluated for the prediction of obstructive CAD and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

43025623.label: Results
43025623.text: Of the 34,761 registry patients, 9,782 (28%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 3.8 years. In the angiographic cohort, 1,597 of 2,869 patients (56%) had obstructive CAD. For the diagnosis of obstructive CAD, the extent of focally impaired myocardium had an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.79), outperforming conventional minimal-segment MFR (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.74, P<0.001), but did not differ significantly from ischemic TPD or physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided the most prognostic information in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 1.32-1.38; C-statistic 0.723), compared with global MFR (C-statistic 0.722) and focally impaired myocardium (C-statistic 0.711).

43025623.label: Conclusion
43025623.text: The extent of focally impaired myocardium by iMFR outperformed conventional MFR for the diagnosis of obstructive CAD but performed similarly to ischemic TPD and physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided more prognostic information than focally impaired myocardium or global MFR.
